questions.q: Why isn't a contract being deployed, verified, and tested (Chapters 1-3) the same as the protocol being healthy right now?
options: A contract can be perfectly correct and still be in the middle of a live incident, like a liquidity crunch or unusual activity concentration
Deployed and verified contracts are mathematically guaranteed to never have incidents
Monitoring is only needed before deployment, never after
Testing and verification automatically prevent all forms of liquidity stress
questions.explain: Correctness and verification are static properties; health is a live, ongoing condition that requires watching real-time activity.

questions.q: For a lending protocol, what does a rising utilization percentage indicate?
options: A growing share of supplied liquidity is borrowed out, which can strain withdrawals if it climbs further
The protocol has become completely risk-free
The smart contract's gas costs are decreasing
Total Value Locked is automatically increasing
questions.explain: Utilization measures how much supplied liquidity is currently borrowed -- high utilization means less liquidity is readily available for withdrawals.

questions.q: Why does a real-time monitoring dashboard surface a wave of related withdrawals faster than a block explorer does?
options: A dashboard aggregates and displays the pattern at a glance, while a block explorer shows one transaction at a time with no aggregation
Block explorers cannot display withdrawal transactions at all
Dashboards and block explorers show exactly the same information in the same format
A dashboard only updates once per day, same as a block explorer
questions.explain: Aggregated, real-time views make patterns across multiple transactions visible immediately, where a block explorer requires manually piecing transactions together.

questions.q: What does 'price deviation' as a monitoring signal refer to?
options: A pool pricing an asset meaningfully away from the rest of the market, which can signal manipulation or a broken oracle
The gas price paid for a single transaction
The difference between a contract's bytecode and its verified source
A scheduled, expected daily price update
questions.explain: When a pool's price diverges significantly from the broader market's price for the same asset, it's a red flag worth investigating.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does Lesson 23 do with the live numbers covered here?
options: Turns these same conditions into alerts that automatically page a human when a threshold is crossed
Ignores them entirely in favor of unrelated testing techniques
Removes the need to ever monitor utilization again
Replaces dashboards with manual, daily block-explorer checks
questions.explain: Lesson 23 builds directly on this lesson's monitoring signals, converting them into automated alert triggers rather than numbers someone has to notice by chance.
